title: Divine Glory and Baptism
english: The face of the one coming with the clouds is a vision that implies a certain emphasis of divine glory and mystery of Christ, as seen by Ezekiel in a firmament with a man seated on a throne, having the appearance of a man, with things above like amber and things below like the appearance of fire, and he placed these things freely at will.

Each of these visions implies a certain emphasis of divine glory and mystery of Christ, and there is nothing preventing us from understanding that the Lord was seen on a light cloud, which fills the type of spiritual rain and dew, and the baptism of salvation, as the blessed Paul says that those from the blood of Israel were baptized in the cloud and in the sea (1 Corinthians 10:2).

The cloud guided those crossing the deep desert, and at night, a pillar of fire was leading, and Christ was written through both, that is, the mystery upon him, namely justification and sanctification in faith and holy baptism.

The Lord had to be seen on a light cloud, clearly and intellectually, in the purification and transformation of the Egyptians, and there was no other way to remove the callus of the deceived soul except through holy baptism, which is why the cloud is established as a type.

Through baptism, we become empowered to cast off the burden of sin, and as we reject ungodliness, we are enabled to think on high things and to lift our hearts up to heavenly things, for we are baptized into the putting away of sin, and in this way, we become, in a certain manner, light and free, as if we had wings.

The image of the Lord sitting on a cloud signifies rest or authority given to us, and Christ rests, not in the worship according to the law, but rather in the perfection that comes through holy baptism, which has made Him the King of those on earth.

The handmade idols of Egypt will be shaken from before His face, for it is written, 'the land is a land of carved images' (Isaiah 30:22 or Ezekiel 20:32), and this will be the result of the holy baptism being revealed and Christ shining forth.
The games of the ancient deceit will be destroyed, and the snares of the devil will be seen as shattered, now that the holy baptism has been revealed and Christ has shone forth.

The entire nation and race, especially the Egyptians, have been led to destruction and perdition due to their deep-seated superstition and deception, for they are the most superstitious, and perhaps surpass the Persians and Assyrians in deception.
The heart of the Egyptians will be defeated, having given way, as I think, because it has surrendered to its own deceit, and this defeat is a direct result of their actions.
translator_notes: The Greek phrase 'ἐπὶ θρόνου δὲ ἄνθρωπον τε- θεᾶσθαι' is translated as 'a man seated on a throne' in the first sentence.
The numerical value '165 νεφελῶν' is not directly relevant to the translation and is thus not included in the English text.

The final sentence of the source is rendered literally, with 'having given way' translating the participial clause 'παραχωρήσασαν', which indicates the cause of the defeat, and 'as I think' translating 'ὥς γε οἶμαι', which indicates the author's personal opinion.

The translation of 'ὑπόπτεροι τρόπον τινὰ διὰ τούτου γινόμεθα' as 'we become, in a certain manner, light and free, as if we had wings' is an attempt to convey the sense of the Greek phrase, which is somewhat ambiguous.

title: The Rhinocorourans and the Canaanite Language
english: …We say that the Rhinocorourans are first, and they speak the Canaanite language. They have not changed their speech so much from that of the Egyptians as from that of the Syrians. Some say that in their own writings they clearly recall Joseph, noting that after having departed from the land of the Jews, he was honored with the priesthood according to the law, having been a tax collector named Ionias in the territories of Levi and in the Canaanite cities, having taken possession of these five cities by contending with some of his own kin, or perhaps having remained under persecution.

This man, they say, having led an uncountable multitude of Jews, settled in one of these five cities, which is also called the city of Asedek, that is, the city of righteousness. From there, they say, they settled near the borders of the Egyptians and loved to speak in the Canaanite language. They will also learn to swear by the name of the Lord. This, too, is paradoxical. For it is the custom of vain worshipers to make an oath by whatever element of the world each one deems important. Some name the heaven, others the sun, and others even the handmade objects in the groves; yet they remember the true God in no way, for they have not known Him.

For those who have already come to know and believe, it is also the custom to swear by His name. In this same way, the all-wise Moses, having led the Israelites out of the worship in Egypt toward the knowledge of the true God, provided for them by saying: "You shall fear the Lord your God, and Him alone shall you serve" (Deuteronomy 6:13). He added to this that they should also swear by His name. This is a clear proof for accepting the faith: that they would take possession of these five cities, not by swearing upon something vain, but rather accepting the need for an oath by the name of the Lord.

On that day, there shall be an altar to the Lord in the land of Egypt, and a pillar at its border to the Lord; and it shall be a sign to the Lord in the land of Egypt. For the whole land of the Egyptians is filled with temples and altars; sacrifices and libations are offered everywhere. This is offered to the elements of the world, and, as I have said, also to the images established in the groves, and even to the pillars of demons. And why do I say this, when they even grant a divine honor to the forms of irrational animals? See then into what things the Egyptian affairs have fallen. For the ancients, being more superstitious than all others, and having wandered recklessly into excess, will, it is said, on that day—that is, in that time—receive the worship of the Lord when the saving proclamation shines upon them…
translator_notes: The text ends mid-sentence with '...τῇ φύσει τε'.
The phrase 'ἐν τοῖς ἐξαίμασι τοῦ Λευῒ' is translated as 'in the territories of Levi' to correct the previous error regarding 'blood'.
The list of elements includes 'τὸν οὐρανὸν' (the heaven), 'τὸν ἥλιον' (the sun), and 'τὰ ἐν σηκοῖς χειρότευκτα' (the handmade objects in the groves).

title: Assyrian Anxiety and the Lament of the Self
english: I have sinned by failing to listen, I have rushed ahead by refusing to look. My heart drifts astray, and lawlessness washes over me like a baptism, my soul has risen up into terror.

For the Assyrian enters, and fearing the road, and not having ignored the enemy's phalanxes, and upon which of them the aim of the war. Not for others, but for me, he says, the Elamites and the picked of the Persians have rushed.
Therefore I will now groan and exhort myself. For those who have come to pass in extreme misfortune seem to need a way of consolation, to lament and to wail. For the tear is melted from grief.

But a thing strange if Assyrians lament, hardened and unfeeling having become always, swollen with pride against all nations, and thinking to possess not an easy resistance. But the bold thus and in their thoughts exceeding man, receive the tear as womanly, and they accomplish lamentation upon themselves, before the trial of the war bending toward weakness.
For my loins have been filled with dissolution, and labor pains…
